what: Why Poisson as the main model?
title: Complete Analysis Workflow
text: Despite NB often better AIC/BIC (reflecting genuine overdispersion), Poisson model recommended primary specification several reasons: Consistency. Poisson PML consistent conditional mean long E(mi|Xi)E(m_i | X_i) correctly specified, regardless true variance function. NB requires correct specification mean variance. Robustness. HC-robust standard errors correct overdispersion Poisson model without adding extra parameter must estimated. Stability. NB model’s joint estimation gamma theta can numerically fragile many observations zero. two-stage approach mitigates introduces conditioning step. NB results serve useful robustness check population size estimate.

title: Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for Population Size — bootstrap_popsize
text: object "uncounted" object (fitted model). R Number bootstrap replications (default 199). cluster One-sided formula cluster variable (e.g., ~ country_code). provided, FWB weights generated cluster level (observations cluster get weight). NULL, observation-level FWB used. level Confidence level (default 0.95). ci_type Type bootstrap CI: "perc" (percentile), "bc" (bias-corrected percentile), "cheap" (Lam, 2022), keeps nominal coverage replications needs spread around plug-estimate: \(\exp\{\log\hat\xi \pm t_{R, 1-/2} S\}\) \(S^2 = R^{-1}\sum_r (\log\hat\xi^*_r - \log\hat\xi)^2\), computed log scale interval stays positive. Useful refits slow; R can small 1, "perc"/"bc" need least 10 converged replications. Default "perc". point_estimate point estimate report: "median" (default, recommended, except ci_type = "cheap" default "plugin") – bootstrap median, robust skewness; "plugin" – plug-\(\hat{\xi} = \sum N^{\hat{\alpha}}\); "mean" – bootstrap mean. seed Random seed reproducibility. verbose Print progress bar? Default TRUE. Optional formula stratified population size estimation (e.g., ~ year, ~ country). provided, bootstrap population sizes computed per -group instead per cov_alpha group. See popsize details. total Logical; TRUE multiple groups exist, include total row computed summing per-replicate group estimates taking quantiles. Default FALSE.

title: Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for Population Size — bootstrap_popsize
text: Fractional weighted bootstrap (FWB). Instead resampling rows, FWB generates random non-negative weights Dirichlet distribution refits model weighted likelihood (Xu et al., 2020). avoids duplicate-row issues discrete data better suited GLMs. fwb package provides implementation. Cluster bootstrap. cluster specified, observations within cluster (e.g., country) receive FWB weight. preserves within-cluster correlation structure (e.g., country observed across multiple years sex categories). Cluster bootstrap recommended whenever observations independent. bootstrap median point estimate. transformation \(\xi = \sum N_i^{\alpha}\) convex \(\alpha\) \(N > 1\), Jensen's inequality \(E[\hat{\xi}] \geq \xi\). bootstrap distribution \(\hat{\xi}\) therefore typically right-skewed, bootstrap mean overestimates \(\xi\). bootstrap median robust central-tendency summary less sensitive skewness, default point estimate. Percentile CI (ci_type = "perc"). interval \([\hat{\xi}^{*}_{\alpha/2}, \; \hat{\xi}^{*}_{1-\alpha/2}]\), .e., \(\alpha/2\) \(1-\alpha/2\) quantiles bootstrap distribution. Bias-corrected percentile CI (ci_type = "bc"). Adjusts quantile probabilities median bias. Let \(z_0 = \Phi^{-1}(\mathrm{Pr}(\hat{\xi}^* < \hat{\xi}_0))\). adjusted quantile probabilities \(p_L = \Phi(2z_0 + z_{\alpha/2})\) \(p_U = \Phi(2z_0 - z_{\alpha/2})\), yielding \([\hat{\xi}^{*}_{p_L}, \; \hat{\xi}^{*}_{p_U}]\). Total across groups. multiple groups exist, total computed summing per-replicate group estimates taking quantiles. correctly accounts -group correlation within bootstrap replicate, unlike summing marginal quantiles.

text: Model specification. observation \(\), expected observed count \(m_i\) modelled : $$E(m_i) = \xi_i \rho_i$$ \(\xi_i = E(M_i \mid N_i)\) theoretical unauthorized population size \(\rho_i = E(p_i \mid N_i, n_i)\) theoretical detection rate. baseline empirical specification, \(\xi_i = N_i^{\alpha_i}\) , default link_rho = "power", \(\rho_i = (\gamma_i + n_i / N_i)^{\beta_i}\). generally, package writes detection component $$\eta_i = \beta_i \log(\gamma_i + n_i / N_i), \qquad \rho_i = h(\eta_i)$$ \(h\) chosen link_rho. text: baseline uncounted mean model factorizes observed-count mean $$\mu_i = E(m_i \mid N_i, n_i) = \xi_i \rho_i,$$ \(\xi_i\) latent population component \(\rho_i\) detection component. default power-link specification, $$ \log \mu_i = \alpha_i \log N_i + \beta_i \log(\gamma + n_i / N_i). $$ helper studies violations identifying assumption introducing omitted shared frailty \(U_i\) log-mean: $$ \log \mu_i^\dagger =   \alpha_i \log N_i +   \beta_i \log(\gamma + n_i / N_i) +   \delta U_i. $$ frailty observed estimated directly. Instead, strength indexed two weighted partial-\(R^2\) quantities: r2_d weighted partial association omitted frailty targeted alpha contrast conditioning fitted nuisance regressors. r2_y weighted partial association omitted frailty working IRLS outcome conditioning targeted contrast nuisance regressors. fitted Poisson NB model, method linearizes mean model working response $$ Y_i^* = \hat\eta_i + \frac{m_i - \hat\mu_i}{\hat\mu_i}, $$ using working weights $$ w_i = \hat\mu_i \qquad \text{(Poisson)} $$ $$ w_i = \frac{\hat\mu_i}{1 + \hat\mu_i / \hat\theta} \qquad \text{(NB2)}. $$ alpha block weighted linearized design \(X_{\alpha,} \log N_i\); beta block \(X_{\beta,} \log(\gamma + n_i/N_i)\). scalar gamma estimated, nuisance design also includes derivative column $$ \frac{\partial \eta_i}{\partial \gamma} = \frac{\hat\beta_i}{\hat\gamma + n_i / N_i}. $$ primary estimand raw alpha coefficient grouped hidden-population estimate $$ \hat\Xi_g = \sum_{\g} N_i^{\hat\alpha_i}. $$ requested group, helper computes gradient \(\hat\Xi_g\) respect alpha-coefficient vector uses gradient define one-dimensional alpha contrast. makes omitted frailty analysis applicable vector-valued cov_alpha models ~ year * ukr + sex. reported contrast internal device: aligns sensitivity calculation direction coefficient space matters chosen \(\Xi_g\). Let \(\theta_g\) denote targeted alpha contrast, estimated standard error \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}(\hat\theta_g)\) degrees freedom \(\nu\). first-order omitted-frailty bias $$ B_{\theta,g}(r2_d, r2_y) = \widehat{\mathrm{se}}(\hat\theta_g) \sqrt{   \nu \frac{r2_y \, r2_d}{1 - r2_d} }. $$ hidden-population effect approximated delta method: $$ \hat\Xi_{g,\mathrm{lower}} \approx \hat\Xi_g - \frac{\partial \Xi_g}{\partial \theta_g} B_{\theta,g}(r2_d, r2_y), $$ $$ \hat\Xi_{g,\mathrm{upper}} \approx \hat\Xi_g + \frac{\partial \Xi_g}{\partial \theta_g} B_{\theta,g}(r2_d, r2_y). $$ returned surface table stores lower/upper approximations raw \(\Xi\) values ratios relative baseline estimate. robustness table summarizes two robustness values threshold questions: rv_equal minimum equal-strength partial-\(R^2\) required omitted frailty move targeted \(\Xi\) requested threshold \(r2_d = r2_y\). rv_extreme corresponding treatment-side strength omitted frailty given extreme outcome-side scenario \(r2_y = 1\). robustness values derived first-order bias mapping. quantify much residual alignment omitted frailty targeted alpha contrast required overturn substantive claim. Interpretation. identification-sensitivity analysis, distinct package's existing distributional sensitivity (method = "nb") bootstrap uncertainty summaries. inspired omitted-variable-bias diagnostics sensemakr, literal OLS port: count model first linearized IRLS working representation, hidden-population estimand handled grouped delta-method contrast. Limitations. method first-order deliberately restricted link_rho = "power", unconstrained Poisson/NB MLE fits without cov_gamma. yet implement benchmark covariates simulation-based calibration layer.
